subject.title: Telegram: Auto-reply to unauthorized group senders with admin contact instructions

question: Should Telegram add an opt-in unauthorized group-sender notice, and what default, rate-limit, raw-ID disclosure, admin-contact, and group-policy semantics should it use?
rationale: The request changes a silent authorization-denial boundary into visible group output and may disclose identifiers or amplify unauthorized traffic, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product/security contract.

options.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default Telegram setting for denied-sender onboarding with per-sender cooldown, thread-safe delivery, admin-contact configuration, and documented raw-ID behavior.

options.title: Use Owner Audit Only
options.body: Keep unauthorized senders silent and route visibility through the broader unauthorized Telegram audit/owner-notification work instead.

options.title: Keep Silent Denial
options.body: Decline sender-facing replies and document groupAllowFrom, logs, and manual ID discovery as the supported secure posture.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In Rate-Limited Notice
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default Telegram setting for denied-sender onboarding with per-sender cooldown, thread-safe delivery, admin-contact configuration, and documented raw-ID behavior.
